reference: GNU coreutils base64, invoked by the system Bash with the same fixture script and a normal system PATH; the documented RFC 4648/GNU behavior is the independent oracle. Candidate execution uses the provided runner with an empty executable PATH.
coverage: Default 76-column wrapping at a line boundary using stdin.
Binary-safe encoding and -w0 output without a final newline.
Custom non-default wrapping and the long --wrap spelling.
Concatenated padded groups and LF-separated input from a relative file.
GNU-compatible unpadded final groups of two and three characters.
Malformed input status, diagnostic presence, and already-decoded output.
Invalid wrap-size status and diagnostic presence.
-- handling for a relative filename beginning with a dash.
exclusions: Not a complete GNU option or diagnostic-wording test; diagnostic text may vary.
Large streaming loads, signals, output-device failures, and locale-specific behavior are outside this bounded suite.

cases.purpose: Check stdin encoding with GNU's default 76-column wrapping when 58 input bytes produce output beyond one line.
Check binary input containing NUL and high bytes with -w0, including the documented absence of a trailing newline.
Check --wrap with a non-default seven-column width, plus long-option width zero and its no-newline behavior.
cases.script: printf 'abcdefghijklmnop' | base64 --wrap=7; printf '|'; printf 'xyz' | base64 --wrap=0; printf '|';

cases.purpose: Check that padded decoding preserves NUL, high-bit, and ordinary bytes exactly.
Check GNU-compatible adjacent padded groups and LF handling when the encoded data comes from a relative file.
Check GNU-compatible incomplete final groups with two and three Base64 characters.
cases.script: printf 'YQ' | base64 -d; printf '|'; printf 'YWI' | base64 -d; printf '|';

cases.purpose: Check long decode and ignore-garbage options with embedded whitespace and punctuation while preserving decoded bytes.
Check that incomplete padding is rejected with nonzero status and a diagnostic after already-decoded bytes are emitted.
Check nonzero status and a diagnostic for a negative --wrap width.
Check -- option termination and opening a relative input file whose name begins with a dash.
Empty encoding/decoding and same-shell decode-to-encode option reset preserve exact bytes.
cases.script:
: > empty
base64 empty
base64 -d empty
printf YQ== > encoded
base64 -d encoded
printf xyz > plain
base64 plain

cases.purpose: A missing private file fails with a diagnostic.
